content: 1. Fosamprenavir affects the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which can increase the levels of sertraline. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended due to the potential for increased toxicity. 2. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of sildenafil by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 3. Fosamprenavir decreases the effects of sitagliptin through mechanisms other than CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Reports suggest hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. 4. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 5. Sodium citrate/citric acid decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate reduces the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Drugs with pH-dependent solubility may require specific recommendations to ensure systemic exposure and efficacy. Administer drugs at least 2 hours before or after sodium zirconium cyclosilicate. 7. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of solifenacin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 8. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of sparsentan by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. No dosage adjustment is needed, but regular monitoring of blood pressure, serum potassium, edema, and kidney function is recommended when sparsentan is coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 9. Stiripentol, a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer, affects fosamprenavir metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates coadministered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects, as dosage adjustments may be required. 10. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of sufentanil SL by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase sufentanil plasma concentrations, potentially leading to prolonged or severe adverse effects, including fatal respiratory depression. 11. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of sunitinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 12. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of tasimelteon by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 14. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer, and sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be monitored for effectiveness when coadministered. 16. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Fosamprenavir and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 18. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Adjust the tezacaftor dosage regimen when coadministered with a strong CYP3A inhibitor. 19. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of theophylline by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of ticagrelor by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ticagrelor is metabolized by CYP3A4/5, and its use with strong CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided. 21. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both fosamprenavir and tipranavir increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 23. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 25. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of toremifene by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Toremifene metabolism may be inhibited by drugs that inhibit CYP3A4 hepatic enzymes. 26. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of trazodone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 27. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 28. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of triazolam by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Ublituximab decreases the effects of fosamprenavir through immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 30. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Vilanterol is a CYP3A4 substrate, and coadministration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 31. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of valbenazine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Reduce the valbenazine dose to 40 mg once daily when coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 32. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of vardenafil by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. The vardenafil dose may need to be reduced when coadministered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 33. Vemurafenib increases the levels of fosamprenavir by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 34. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of verapamil by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Both fluticasone furoate and vilanterol are CYP3A4 substrates, and coadministration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 36. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of voclosporin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 37. Fosamprenavir decreases the levels or effects of warfarin by altering CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 38. Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 39. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Reduce zanubrutinib (a CYP3A4 substrate) to 80 mg PO BID when coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. Interrupt the dose as recommended for adverse reactions. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor, resume the previous dose of zanubrutinib. 40. Fosamprenavir and zidovudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 41. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of zileuton by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised due to the potential for increased toxicity.
